rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## is_well_formed

Test whether a string is **well-formed XML** — returns `true` if it parses, `false` if it is malformed. **Never raises** (unlike the other functions).

**When to use:** validate or filter a column of candidate XML before transforming or querying it, e.g. `WHERE xslt.main.is_well_formed(doc)`, so malformed rows do not abort the scan.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the candidate text). `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `BOOLEAN` — `true` for well-formed XML, `false` for malformed text; NULL input yields NULL.

**Behavior & edge cases:** this checks *well-formedness* (does it parse), not schema validity — SaxonC-HE is not schema-aware, so there is no XSD validation. Well-formedness is the strongest XML check the HE edition offers.
rows.vgi.doc_md: # is_well_formed Return `true` if the text is well-formed XML, `false` if malformed (never errors). ## Usage ```sql SELECT xslt.main.is_well_formed(''); -- true SELECT xslt.main.is_well_formed(''); -- false ``` ## Notes - Checks well-formedness only; there is no XSD/schema validation (HE limitation). - Safe to use in `WHERE` to filter out malformed rows. - NULL input -> NULL output.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Check whether a string is well-formed XML.", "sql": "SELECT xslt.main.is_well_formed('')"}]
rows.vgi.title: Check XML Well-Formedness

rows: One row describing the bundled SaxonC engine: version, edition, and language levels

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## saxon_info

A **single-row reference table** describing the SaxonC engine bundled with this worker: its version, edition, and the XSLT/XQuery/XPath language levels it implements.

**When to use:** discover what the engine can do before you rely on it — most importantly the `schema_aware` flag (always false on the Home Edition, so there is no XSD validation) and the language levels behind `xslt`, `xquery`, and the `xpath_*` functions. Because it takes no arguments, it is directly browsable — the whole table is a single row of engine facts.

**Inputs:** none.

**Output columns:** `version`, `edition`, `xslt_version`, `xquery_version`, `xpath_version` (all `VARCHAR`) and `schema_aware` (`BOOLEAN`).

**Behavior & edge cases:** always exactly one row; the language levels and edition are constant, only `version` is read from the running build.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# saxon_info

A single-row reference table describing the bundled SaxonC engine and the capabilities it exposes to the rest of this catalog.

## Usage

The table has no arguments and a single row: read the `version`, `edition`, and `xslt_version` / `xquery_version` / `xpath_version` columns for the engine facts, and the `schema_aware` column to learn whether XSD validation is available.

## Notes

- Always one row; no arguments, so it is directly browsable.
- `schema_aware` is always false on SaxonC-HE (no XSD validation).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Read the engine version and whether XSD validation is available.", "sql": "SELECT version, schema_aware FROM xslt.main.saxon_info"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "version", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "SaxonC version string of the bundled engine."}, {"name": "edition", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Saxon edition (HE = Home Edition, the free, non-schema-aware build)."}, {"name": "xslt_version", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "XSLT language level the engine implements."}, {"name": "xquery_version", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "XQuery language level the engine implements."}, {"name": "xpath_version", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "XPath language level the engine implements."}, {"name": "schema_aware", "type": "BOOLEAN", "description": "Whether the engine can do XSD validation / schema-aware processing (always false on HE)."}]
rows.vgi.title: Saxon Engine Capabilities

rows: String values of ALL matches of an XPath 3.1 expression, as a list -- UNNEST it to shred one document into rows

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_array

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return the string values of **all matches** as a `VARCHAR[]` list.

**When to use:** shred XML into rows. Apply this to a column of documents and `UNNEST(...)` the result to turn one document into many rows — the per-row counterpart to the `xpath_nodes` table function (which binds one constant document).

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression selecting many items). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR[]` — the string value of every match, in document order; an empty list when nothing matches.

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL (not an empty list). Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: # xpath_array Return the string values of ALL XPath 3.1 matches as a `VARCHAR[]` list. ## Usage ```sql SELECT UNNEST(xslt.main.xpath_array('ab', '//i')); ``` ## Notes - `UNNEST` the list to shred a column of documents into rows. - For a single constant document, the `xpath_nodes` table function is handier. - NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Shred all matching nodes into rows with UNNEST.", "sql": "SELECT UNNEST(xslt.main.xpath_array('ab', '//i'))"}]
rows.vgi.title: XPath Match Array

rows: Effective boolean value of an XPath 3.1 expression over the document

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_boolean

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return its **effective boolean value** (EBV).

**When to use:** test a condition over XML inside a SQL `WHERE`/`CASE` — does a node exist (`boolean(//x)`), does a count match (`count(//a) = 1`), or any predicate that XPath can express.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `BOOLEAN` — the EBV of the expression (a non-empty node-set is true, an empty one is false; numeric/string EBV rules apply for atomics).

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# xpath_boolean

Return the effective boolean value of an XPath 3.1 expression over a document.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT xslt.main.xpath_boolean('<r><a/></r>', 'count(//a) = 1');  -- true
```

## Notes

- Follows XPath effective-boolean-value rules (existence, numbers, strings).
- NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Test an XPath count predicate as a boolean.", "sql": "SELECT xslt.main.xpath_boolean('<r><a/></r>', 'count(//a) = 1')"}]
rows.vgi.title: XPath Boolean Test

rows: One (seq, value) row per XPath 3.1 match in a single document

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_nodes

Explode a single XML document into rows: emit **one `(seq, value)` row per XPath 3.1 match**, in document order.

**When to use:** shred one constant document into a relational result — turn `//item` matches into a numbered table you can join, filter, and aggregate. For shredding a *column* of documents instead, use the `xpath_array` scalar with `UNNEST`.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`; table-function named-argument syntax (`name := value`) is supported.

**Output columns:** `seq` (`BIGINT`, 1-based position) and `value` (`VARCHAR`, the match's string value).

**Behavior & edge cases:** no matches -> zero rows. Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# xpath_nodes

Table function: one `(seq, value)` row per XPath 3.1 match in one document.

## Usage

Call `xslt.main.xpath_nodes(xml, expr)` in a `FROM` clause to expand each match into a numbered `(seq, value)` row.

## Notes

- Binds a single constant document; use `xpath_array` + `UNNEST` per row.
- `seq` is the 1-based document-order position of each match.
- Invalid XML/XPath raises an error.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Number each XPath match and return it in document order.", "sql": "SELECT seq, value FROM xslt.main.xpath_nodes('ab', '//i') ORDER BY seq"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "seq", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "1-based position of the match in document/sequence order."}, {"name": "value", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "String value of the matched node/item."}]
rows.vgi.title: XPath Nodes Table

Numeric (`DOUBLE`) value of the first XPath 3.1 match (NULL if non-numeric)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_number

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return its **numeric value** as a `DOUBLE`.

**When to use:** extract a number from XML and use it in SQL arithmetic — a measurement, a count (`count(//item)`), a sum (`sum(//price)`), or any numeric XPath computation.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `DOUBLE` — the numeric value of the first match, or NULL when the value is non-numeric (XPath NaN) or nothing matches.

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. Wrap a path in `number(...)` to coerce a text node. Malformed XML or XPath raises a clean DuckDB error.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# xpath_number

Return the numeric (`DOUBLE`) value of the first XPath 3.1 match, or NULL.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT xslt.main.xpath_number('<r><n>42</n></r>', 'number(//n)');  -- 42.0
```

## Notes

- Non-numeric results (XPath NaN) come back as NULL.
- Use XPath aggregates like `count(...)` / `sum(...)` directly.
- NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Read a numeric value out of the document via XPath.", "sql": "SELECT xslt.main.xpath_number('<r><n>42</n></r>', 'number(//n)')"}]
rows.vgi.title: XPath Numeric Value

rows: String value of the first node/atomic matching an XPath 3.1 expression (NULL if none)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xpath_string

Evaluate an **XPath 3.1** expression against an XML document and return the **string value of the first match** (or NULL when nothing matches).

**When to use:** pull a single text value out of XML — an element's text, an attribute, or any atomic computed by XPath (`string(...)`, `concat(...)`, etc.).

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document) and `expr` (an XPath 3.1 expression). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR` — the string value of the first node/atomic in document order, or NULL if the expression selects nothing.

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. A malformed document or a malformed XPath raises a clean DuckDB error. Namespaces follow the document's in-scope bindings; use `//*:name` or `local-name()` predicates for namespace-agnostic matching.
rows.vgi.doc_md: # xpath_string Return the string value of the first XPath 3.1 match in a document, or NULL. ## Usage ```sql SELECT xslt.main.xpath_string('x', '//a'); -- 'x' ``` ## Notes - Returns the FIRST match only; use `xpath_array` to collect all matches. - NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/XPath raises an error. - Namespace-agnostic matching: `//*:tag` or `local-name() = 'tag'`.
rows.vgi.title: XPath String Value

rows: Run an XQuery 3.1 query with the document as context item; returns the serialized result

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xquery

Run an **XQuery 3.1** query against an XML document (bound as the context item) and return the serialized result.

**When to use:** richer querying than a single XPath — FLWOR expressions (`for`/`let`/`where`/`order by`/`return`), constructed elements, joins across parts of the document, and string/sequence functions like `string-join(//i, ',')`.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document, available as `.` and `/`) and `query` (the XQuery 3.1 source). Both `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR` — the serialized query result (atomic text, or constructed XML, depending on the query).

**Behavior & edge cases:** NULL in either argument yields NULL. Use `xquery_rows` instead when you want one row per item of the result sequence. Malformed XML or a malformed query raises a clean DuckDB error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: # xquery Run an XQuery 3.1 query with the document as the context item; returns the serialized result. ## Usage ```sql SELECT xslt.main.xquery('ab', 'string-join(//i, ",")'); ``` ## Notes - The document is the context item (`.` / `/`). - For a result sequence, `xquery_rows` returns one row per item. - NULL input -> NULL output; invalid XML/query raises an error.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Join matched values into one string with an XQuery string-join.", "sql": "SELECT xslt.main.xquery('ab', 'string-join(//i, \",\")')"}]
rows.vgi.title: Run XQuery Query

rows: One (seq, value) row per item in an XQuery 3.1 result sequence

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xquery_rows

Run an **XQuery 3.1** query against one document and emit **one `(seq, value)` row per item** of the result sequence, in sequence order.

**When to use:** when the query yields a sequence (e.g. a FLWOR `for $x in //i return $x*2`) and you want each item as its own row to join, filter, or aggregate in SQL. Use the `xquery` scalar instead when you want the whole result serialized into one value.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the document, bound as the context item) and `expr` (the XQuery 3.1 source). Both `VARCHAR`; named-argument syntax supported.

**Output columns:** `seq` (`BIGINT`, 1-based position) and `value` (`VARCHAR`, the item's string value).

**Behavior & edge cases:** an empty result sequence -> zero rows. Malformed XML or a malformed query raises a clean DuckDB error.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# xquery_rows

Table function: one `(seq, value)` row per item in an XQuery 3.1 result sequence.

## Usage

Call `xslt.main.xquery_rows(xml, expr)` in a `FROM` clause to expand each item of the result sequence into a numbered `(seq, value)` row.

## Notes

- One row per sequence item; `seq` is the 1-based position.
- Use the `xquery` scalar for a single serialized result.
- Invalid XML/query raises an error.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Explode an XQuery FLWOR result into numbered rows.", "sql": "SELECT seq, value FROM xslt.main.xquery_rows('12', 'for $x in //i return $x*2') ORDER BY seq"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "seq", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "1-based position of the match in document/sequence order."}, {"name": "value", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "String value of the matched node/item."}]
rows.vgi.title: XQuery Rows Table

Transform an XML document with an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet; returns the serialized result

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
## xslt

Apply an **XSLT 3.0** stylesheet to an XML document and return the serialized transformation result as text.

**When to use:** reshape, rename, filter, or compute over XML — the full power of XSLT 3.0 (templates, `xsl:value-of`, `xsl:for-each`, modes, functions) — directly in SQL.

**Inputs:** `xml` (the source document) and `stylesheet` (the XSLT 3.0 source). Both are `VARCHAR`.

**Output:** `VARCHAR` — the serialized result tree (often XML, but the stylesheet's `xsl:output` may select text/HTML/JSON).

**Behavior & edge cases:** a NULL in either argument yields NULL for that row. Malformed XML or a malformed stylesheet raises a clean DuckDB error. A constant stylesheet down a column compiles once and is reused. SaxonC-HE is not schema-aware, so schema-aware (validating) XSLT is unavailable.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# xslt

Transform an XML document with an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, returning the serialized result.

## Usage

Call `xslt.main.xslt(xml, stylesheet)` in any projection to transform a document column against a stylesheet.

## Notes

- Powered by SaxonC-HE (XSLT 3.0).
- NULL input -> NULL output.
- Invalid XML or stylesheet raises a DuckDB error.
- A constant stylesheet is compiled once and reused across rows.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Apply an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, lifting an inner element value into a new wrapper element.", "sql": "SELECT xslt.main.xslt('<doc><n>hi</n></doc>', '<xsl:stylesheet version=\"3.0\" xmlns:xsl=\"http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform\"><xsl:template match=\"/\"><out><xsl:value-of select=\"//n\"/></out></xsl:template></xsl:stylesheet>')"}]
rows.vgi.executable_examples: [{"description": "Apply an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, lifting an inner element value into a new wrapper element.", "sql": "SELECT xslt.main.xslt('<doc><n>hi</n></doc>', '<xsl:stylesheet version=\"3.0\" xmlns:xsl=\"http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform\"><xsl:template match=\"/\"><out><xsl:value-of select=\"//n\"/></out></xsl:template></xsl:stylesheet>')"}]
rows.vgi.title: Apply XSLT Stylesheet
